record.original_question: For each of the semigroup conjugacy relations ∼o, ∼tr, ∼p∗, ∼n, and ∼u, what is the largest natural number n for which intersecting that relation with Green’s H-relation always gives exactly subgroup conjugacy ∼g on every semigroup with at most n elements?

evidence.quote: Problem 9.1. For each ∼ ∈ {∼o, ∼tr, ∼p∗, ∼n, ∼u}, what is the largest n ∈ N such that ∼ ∩ H = ∼g for all semigroups with at most n elements?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let S be a semigroup and let S¹ denote S with an identity adjoined (if S has none). Recall Green's relation ℋ on S, defined by a ℋ b iff aS¹ = bS¹ and S¹a = S¹b.

For elements a,b ∈ S, define the following five "conjugacy" relations:

(1) Otto's conjugacy ∼_o: a ∼_o b iff there exist g,h ∈ S¹ such that ag = gb and bh = ha.

(2) Trace/representation conjugacy ∼_tr: a ∼_tr b iff a and b have, in their respective subgroups generated by idempotent powers of themselves (when a, b are in epigroup-like position), conjugate group parts via the standard trace conjugacy definition; equivalently, a ∼_tr b iff some power a^n lies in a maximal subgroup G_e and some power b^m lies in a maximal subgroup G_f with e ℋ-related to f and the group-parts conjugate inside that group.

(3) The transitive closure ∼_{p*} of the primary conjugacy ∼_p, where a ∼_p b iff a = uv and b = vu for some u,v ∈ S¹.

(4) Konieczny's conjugacy ∼_n: a ∼_n b iff there exist g,h ∈ S¹ with ag = gb, bh = ha, hag = b, and gbh = a.

(5) Unit conjugacy ∼_u: a ∼_u b iff there exists u in the group of units U(S) of S (assumed nonempty) with u⁻¹au = b and ubu⁻¹ = a.

Let ∼_g denote subgroup conjugacy: a ∼_g b iff a and b lie in a common subgroup G of S and g·a·g⁻¹ = b for some g ∈ G.

For each ∼ ∈ {∼_o, ∼_tr, ∼_{p*}, ∼_n, ∼_u}, determine the largest natural number n such that the equality ∼ ∩ ℋ = ∼_g holds in every semigroup of cardinality at most n.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem (Problem 9.1) in a recent semigroup-theory work cataloguing the interaction of various semigroup conjugacy notions with Green's ℋ relation. A subsequent preprint by Trevor Jack ("Answering Five Open Problems Involving Semigroup Conjugacy") addresses several open problems from this line of work, but no source located confirms a definitive value for the largest n in this specific question across all five relations. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Answering Five Open Problems Involving Semigroup Conjugacy (arXiv abstract)
status_evidence.snippet: Paper discusses conjugacy relations ∼o, ∼c, ∼n, ∼p, ∼p*, ∼tr in semigroups and addresses several open problems but does not explicitly state a final answer to the largest-n problem.
status_evidence.claim: Related work targets open problems on semigroup conjugacy without giving a confirmed final answer to the largest-n statement of Problem 9.1.

status_evidence.title: Conjugation in Semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational paper introducing several of the semigroup conjugacy relations referenced in Problem 9.1.
status_evidence.claim: Definitions of ∼o, ∼p, ∼n etc. originate in this and related work; the comparison with ℋ ∩ ∼g remains an active research topic.
